title: Regional blackout and black start · Sør-Rogaland
description: A summer weekday evening, 18:00. The 132 kV network serving southern Stavanger, Sandnes and Ryfylke is fed from the transmission grid through two transformers, Lyse 300/132 kV and Fagrafjell 420/132 kV. At this hour Elhub's measured summer demand and the area's measured production put the region at about 300 MW, about 60 % of it imported. The Grid starts from the summer night's unit commitment, with the evening's extra demand shared over the online units' headroom. One minute in, both transformers trip. The region's own units cannot carry the deficit: its frequency collapses within a second, every unit trips and the island goes dead while the rest of the grid stays live. Restore it as a black-start exercise: a dead island energises only from a black-start capable unit inside it or by closing a branch onto it from a live neighbour, and the exercise keeps both transformers open until the region is live again. Lysebotn I (120 MW), Flørli and Jøssang are the region's units the model marks black-start capable, by its rule for storage hydropower (Statnett does not publish its black-start providers). Disconnect the demand, black-start Lysebotn I onto a small starting block, pick up the rest in blocks small enough to stay above the 48.8 Hz first stage of under-frequency load shedding, then bring the island within 0.1 Hz of the main grid and close a transformer under synchro-check. There are no weather-driven faults.
objectives: Confirm the blackout: the region's island is de-energised, its units are tripped and its demand is out, while the main grid stays live (islands.list, assets.search with the island id).

Prepare the black start: reset Lysebotn I's trip and disconnect the region's demand with emergency shedding (shed-load with emergency: true), leaving a starting block of about 45 MW in Ryfylke and Gjesdal (Forsand, Dalen, Jøssang, Nye Veland, Nye Hjelmeland and the Fagrafjell 132 kV bus) for Lysebotn I's 36 MW minimum stable output. A unit that is not black-start capable cannot start in the dead island.
Black-start Lysebotn I (start-generator): after its five-minute start-up it energises the island and carries the starting block.

Pick up the Stavanger and Sandnes demand in blocks of about 10 MW, raising Lysebotn I's set-point with each block and letting the frequency recover between blocks, so that no under-frequency load-shedding stage operates.

Resynchronise: close-branch refuses a transformer while the island and the main grid differ by more than 0.1 Hz. Trim Lysebotn I's set-point in small steps, close the Fagrafjell transformer once the frequencies agree, then close the Lyse transformer and restore the remaining demand from the main grid.

guidance.title: Sør-Rogaland hangs on two transformers
guidance.message: The authored model imports power through the Lyse and Fagrafjell transformers and schedules both trips at +1 min. Use the expert Guide or inspect present demand, island state and supplies before advancing.

guidance.title: Inspect the island and begin restoration
guidance.message: Inspect both transformer states, the island energisation and cue outcomes. If the intended islanding occurred, keep the transformers open while building a viable load block, starting Lysebotn I, picking up load and resynchronising under the actual synchro-check. Read back achieved frequency and supply at each stage.

guide.title: Restore a de-energised island
guide.description: Expert grid exercise. Use actual island state, viable load blocks and synchro-check feedback.

steps.title: Inspect the starting system
steps.instruction: Open Grid operations and inspect the Rogaland island, supplies and load blocks before the one-minute transformer event.

steps.title: Reach the islanding event
steps.instruction: Advance one simulation minute and inspect actual de-energisation and transformer outcomes.

steps.title: Build a viable starting block
steps.instruction: Inspect current demand, isolate an appropriately small block and reset/start the correct black-start unit using supported controls. Read back actual energisation and frequency; a start command alone is insufficient.

steps.title: Pick up load in small blocks
steps.instruction: Add compatible load blocks gradually while reading current frequency, generation margin and rejected controls. Pause to diagnose each refusal rather than retrying a full region at once.

steps.title: Resynchronise from evidence
steps.instruction: Inspect voltage, angle and frequency across the connection. Use the real synchro-check control and verify its accepted/denied result and subsequent power flow.

steps.title: Review remaining restoration
steps.instruction: Inspect residual unserved load, tripped generation and reserves. Report achieved restoration with times and remaining constraints. This guide never certifies restoration from acknowledgement alone.

steps.title: Continue exploring
steps.instruction: This guide is finished. The same Run remains available. Pause or stop guidance whenever you wish; those controls do not pause the shared simulation. Copy the Run before trying a different intervention. Acknowledgements record your choice to continue, not a qualification.
